newsitem.title: THAILAND: U.S. says Asia response key to WTO talks success.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Asia response key to WTO talks success.

text.p: The United States said on Monday the success of the December World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore hinged on Asian responses to anticipated European and American trade concessions.

Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang told reporters that the European Union, U.S. and probably Japan and Canada were expected to make concessions on telecomunications foreign ownership and competition soon.
A reciprocal response was required from Asian nations.
Mr Lang said: "The WTO telecoms services agreement negotiations cannot succeeed without market-opening committments from the high-growth countries of Asia."

"In those areas the focus which had previously been on the European Union will switch to Asia and particularly to the ASEAN region," he added. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups seven countries.

He said existing responses from Asian countries were disappointing: "Some governments have made no offers, some governments have made weak offers but there are really no strong offers here in asia. I don't think negotiations can succeed on that basis."

Other concessions agreed by trade ministers from the EU, the United States and Japan, included the introduction of zero tariffs on semiconductors by the turn of the century and liberalisation of related hi-technology sectors.
Other issues due for discussion in December were the potentially thorny discussions on the transparency of government purchasing and limited talks on labour standards.
The WTO's deadline for liberalisation of the the telecommunication sector is February 15 1997, the deadline for liberalisation of the finance sector is December 1997.
